historical_references.reference: Ibn Khaldun's 'Muqaddimah' mentions a tribe called Banu Samik, who inhabited the Maghreb region around the 13th century.
historical_references.context: Ibn Khaldun was a famous historian and sociologist from Tunisia, whose work 'Muqaddimah' provides valuable insights into medieval North African history. The Banu Samik are mentioned in this work as a powerful and influential Berber tribe that controlled significant parts of the Maghreb during this period.

historical_references.reference: Al-Bakri describes the Samik as a great Berber confederation in the Fez region during the Almoravid period (11th-12th centuries).
historical_references.context: Al-Bakri was a geographer and traveler from Seville, Spain, who wrote extensively about North Africa and its peoples. In his work 'Al-Maslik wal-Mamalik', he mentions the Samik as a powerful Berber confederation that controlled the Fez region during the Almoravid period. They were known for their military strength and strategic alliances.
